fact: 1923年1月11日，法国与比利时军队（最初约6万人，后增至10万人）在法国将军让·德古特指挥下占领鲁尔工业区，最东至多特蒙德。法国立即接管民政管理，协约国工厂矿山监督代表团（MICUM，由72名法、比、意专家组成）随军进驻，以核实冶炼厂与矿井的赔偿交付能力。英国政府认定占领为非法，美国政府谴责其为「强权政策」。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Occupation of the Ruhr
sources.quote: Between 11 and 16 January 1923, French and Belgian troops under the command of French General Jean Degoutte, initially numbering 60,000 men and later climbing to 100,000, occupied the entire Ruhr area as far east as Dortmund. The French immediately took over civil administration from the Germans. ... MICUM consisted of 72 French, Belgian and Italian experts, most of whom were engineers. ... The government of the United Kingdom categorised the occupation of the Ruhr as illegal. The United States government condemned the occupation as a reprehensible "policy of force".

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, France Occupies the Ruhr
sources.quote: On January 11, 1923, Poincaré dispatched a technical mission and two army divisions to Essen, the headquarters of the German Coal Syndicate. The Belgian government assisted the operation with a token number of troops. The stated purpose of the mission was to ensure that coal and timber deliveries were made according to schedule.

fact: 1923年1月13日，德国帝国议会以283票对12票通过决议，将「消极抵抗」（passive resistance）确认为正式政策：官员不得与占领当局合作，赔偿物资交付停止，古诺政府补贴停工的工厂与矿井、支付罢工工人工资，资金来源是印钞。到5月，鲁尔约40万工人罢工。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Occupation of the Ruhr
sources.quote: Chancellor Cuno immediately encouraged the passive resistance, and on January 13, the Reichstag voted 283 to 12 to approve it as a formal policy. Officials were told not to cooperate with the occupying forces, and deliveries of reparation material were stopped.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Weimar Republic
sources.quote: The German government under Chancellor Wilhelm Cuno responded with a policy of non-violent passive resistance to the occupation. It underwrote the costs of idled factories and mines and paid the workers who were on strike. Unable to meet the enormous costs by any other means, it resorted to printing money.

fact: 1923年8月10日柏林印刷业罢工开始，在德共推动下扩展到政府印钞厂，纸币印刷机停转导致现金立即短缺。罢工蔓延至汉堡、卢萨蒂亚、萨克森与图林根等地，总计约350万工人参加。8月12日社会民主党在帝国议会提出不信任案，古诺内阁辞职。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Cuno strikes
sources.quote: A labour dispute in the Berlin printing industry triggered a strike on 10 August 1923. At the instigation of the Communist Party (KPD), it expanded to include the government printing plant. The shutdown of the banknote presses led to an immediate shortage of paper money. ... In total, three-and-a-half million workers went on strike, indirectly forcing Cuno and his cabinet to resign. In addition to the pressure from the strikes, the SPD introduced a vote of no confidence in the Reichstag against the Cuno government, which resigned on 12 August.

fact: 1923年8月13日，古斯塔夫·斯特雷泽曼出任总理，主持「百日内阁」。9月26日正式宣布终止「消极抵抗」政策；此前9月20日英法首脑重申合作使斯特雷泽曼确认无法指望英国向法国施压。此后煤业辛迪加开始与法、比谈判。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Weimar Republic
sources.quote: Realizing that continuing the course was untenable, the new Reich Chancellor Gustav Stresemann called off the passive resistance in September 1923.

sources.title: 快懂百科，魏玛共和国
sources.quote: 9月20日,英法首脑对双方合作的再次强调,让斯特雷泽曼意识到无法指望英国向法国施压,于是在26日正式宣布停止「消极抵抗」政策。接着,魏玛共和国的煤业辛迪加在政府支持下同法、比谈判。

fact: 1923年11月8日至9日，阿道夫·希特勒与埃里希·鲁登道夫在慕尼黑啤酒馆发动政变（Beer Hall Putsch），试图推翻魏玛政府。政变被巴伐利亚当局与国防军镇压，暴动失败，但纳粹党由此进入全国政治视野。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Weimar Republic
sources.quote: On 8 November 1923, in a pact with Erich Ludendorff, a league of nationalist fighting societies called the Kampfbund, took over a meeting that Kahr and Lossow were holding at a beer hall in Munich. Ludendorff and Hitler declared that the Weimar government was deposed and that they were planning to take control of Munich the following day. Kahr and Lossow organized the resistance to Hitler, with the result that the coup attempt was easily stopped.

fact: 1923年11月15日，地租马克（Rentenmark）正式投入流通，取代帝国银行发行的废纸马克；价格标签去掉12个零后，以新货币标价的价格保持稳定。11月12日沙赫特出任货币专员后，帝国银行被禁止再贴现政府国库券。11月20日帝国银行行长哈芬施坦因心脏病突发去世，沙赫特接任行长。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic
sources.quote: On 16 November 1923, the new Rentenmark was introduced to replace the worthless paper marks issued by the Reichsbank. Twelve zeros were cut from prices, and the prices quoted in the new currency remained stable. When the president of the Reichsbank, Rudolf Havenstein, died on 20 November 1923, Schacht was appointed to replace him.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Reichsbank
sources.quote: By decree of 15 October 1923 on the initiative of finance minister Hans Luther, the government created a separate bank, the Deutsche Rentenbank, endowed with the right to issue notes redeemable in a kind of non-interest-bearing mortgage bond, the Rentenbrief, denominated in gold Mark and theoretically backed by a collective mortgage debt imposed upon German agriculture and industry.

fact: 1923年10月23日至25日，汉堡共产党组织武装起义（汉堡起义），在恩斯特·台尔曼领导下与警察发生武装冲突，终因力量悬殊于10月25日撤出战斗。11月，共产党组织千余人被捕判刑。10月中旬萨克森与图林根成立包含左翼社民党与共产党人的政府，月底被国防军依据魏玛宪法第48条以「帝国执行」解散。

sources.title: 快懂百科，魏玛共和国
sources.quote: 10月23日,汉堡的共产党组织举行武装起义,但未能鼓动起广泛的罢工和武装起义,终因力量悬殊于10月25日撤出战斗。11月,共产党组织千余人被捕判刑。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Weimar Republic
sources.quote: In Saxony and Thuringia, Communists won enough seats to participate in governments under Social Democratic minister presidents. In both states the Communists were expelled by Reich executions (Reichsexekutionen) using Article 48 of the Weimar Constitution.

fact: 柏林一条面包的价格从1922年底约160纸马克涨到1923年底的2000亿纸马克。到1923年11月，1美元可兑换4.2105万亿德国马克。工人每天发两次工资以便赶在下一轮涨价前花掉；货币替代物（香烟、物物交换）广泛流通。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic
sources.quote: A loaf of bread in Berlin that cost around 160 marks at the end of 1922 cost 200 billion marks by late 1923. By November 1923, one US dollar was worth 4.2105 trillion German marks.

sources.title: ConvexTrade, Hyperinflation
sources.quote: At the peak, prices doubled every 3.7 days. Workers were paid twice daily with wheelbarrows of cash and raced to spend it before the next price increase. A loaf of bread cost 200 billion marks.

sources.title: ConvexTrade, Hyperinflation（Weimar Germany汇率与价格指数表）
海外网，德国恶性通胀的教训
sources.quote: 失业率于10月达到了19.1%,11月23.4%,12月则是28.2%。恶性通货膨胀使绝大多数的德国人状况恶化,尤其是中产阶级。

fact: 1923年2月24日，帝国议会通过授权法，赋予古诺政府「采取一切必要措施抵抗法国」的权力，但古诺较少动用。斯特雷泽曼上台后频繁使用魏玛宪法第48条紧急法令治国。10月萨克森、图林根的左翼联合政府被第48条「帝国执行」解散。紧急状态与行政法令构成1923年德国日常法律环境的核心。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Occupation of the Ruhr
sources.quote: The Reichstag, recognizing that the extraordinary nature of the event could not be met using normal parliamentary measures, passed an enabling act on 24 February. It gave the Cuno government the power to use all necessary measures to resist the French, but Cuno made relatively little use of it.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Weimar Republic
sources.quote: In both states the Communists were expelled by Reich executions (Reichsexekutionen) using Article 48 of the Weimar Constitution.

fact: 法国占领当局对消极抵抗的德国人判处12万至15万项刑罚，绝大多数是驱逐出鲁尔与莱茵兰到德国未占领区，部分为监禁。蒂森钢铁公司老板弗里茨·蒂森因拒绝交付煤炭被捕；克虏伯公司老板古斯塔夫·克虏伯被判处15年监禁并罚款1亿马克（后仅服刑7个月即被释放）。法国还在鲁尔与德国其余地区之间设立封锁线，20万至30万营养不良的儿童被疏散出鲁尔。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Occupation of the Ruhr
sources.quote: French authorities imposed between 120,000 and 150,000 sentences against resisting Germans. Some involved prison sentences, but the overwhelming majority were deportations from the Ruhr district and the Rhineland to the unoccupied part of Germany. Among those arrested were Fritz Thyssen of the Thyssen steel company for his refusal to deliver coal and Gustav Krupp ... Krupp was sentenced to fifteen years in prison and fined 100 million marks, but he served only seven months and was released when passive resistance was called off. ... between 200,000 and 300,000 undernourished or starving children were evacuated from the Ruhr.

fact: 1923年10月13日至15日的货币改革法令设立地租银行（Deutsche Rentenbank），发行地租马克（Rentenmark），以对农业、工业和商业地產征收的集体抵押债务为担保，黄金债券按每公斤黄金2790金马克（战前平价）指数化。地租马克不可兑换黄金，仅与黄金债券挂钩。发行上限为32亿地租马克。1地租马克=1万亿纸马克，对美元约4.2:1（战前平价）。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic
sources.quote: The plan was adopted in monetary reform decrees on 13–15 October 1923. A new bank, the Rentenbank, was set up by Hans Luther when he became Finance Minister. ... Rentenmarks were not redeemable in gold but only indexed to the gold bonds. ... No fixed exchange rate was set by law, but the "Rentenmark" became interchangeable with paper Mark at the rate of one to one trillion. The Rentenmark was thus in effect a transitory domestic currency, which was never convertible internationally.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Reichsbank
sources.quote: That confidence-building initiative succeeded against all expectations, even though the Rentenbankscheine only had the status of "legally admitted medium of exchange" while the Reichsbank's devalued paper notes remained legal tender. No fixed exchange rate was set by law, but the "Rentenmark" became interchangeable with paper Mark at the rate of one to one trillion. The Rentenmark was thus in effect a transitory domestic currency, which was never convertible internationally.

fact: 帝国银行的贴现率在1923年11月恶性通胀顶点时达到每天40%。11月12日沙赫特出任货币专员后，帝国银行被禁止继续贴现政府国库券，纸马克发行停止；商业票据贴现仍被允许，地租马克的发行严格控制在与当前商业和政府交易相适应的水平。地租银行拒绝向政府和无法借到地租马克的投机者放贷，因为地租马克不是法偿货币。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Reichsbank
sources.quote: The Reichsbank only started raising its discount rate in July 1922, reaching 40 percent per day at the hyperinflationary peak in November 1923. ... After 12 November 1923, when Hjalmar Schacht became currency commissioner, Germany's central bank (the Reichsbank) was not allowed to discount any further government Treasury bills, which meant the corresponding issue of paper marks also ceased. ... The Rentenbank refused credit to the government and to speculators who were not able to borrow Rentenmarks, because Rentenmarks were not legal tender.

fact: 恶性通胀使固定收益资产归零：储蓄、养老金、保险金的实际价值几乎消失；同时固定债务也随货币贬值而化为乌有。拥有土地或房屋的中产阶级业主因债务随货币贬值而实际获益；大型工业企业（如胡戈·施廷内斯的1535家企业帝国）同样通过负债扩张获利，财富向少数人集中。施廷内斯帝国在1923年11月15日地租马克引入后崩溃。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Weimar Republic
sources.quote: While personal savings became virtually worthless, so did fixed debts. Middle class owners of land or houses often came out ahead because their debts lost value along with the currency. Large industrial concerns profited in the same manner, and wealth concentrated in fewer hands. The classic example was Hugo Stinnes, who earned the title of Inflation King by taking advantage of its effects on debt to amass controlling interests in 1,535 businesses with 2,890 different plants by 1924. Stinnes' empire collapsed after the government-sponsored inflation was stopped by the introduction of the Rentenmark on 15 November 1923.

fact: 恶性通胀末期，纸马克信用全面崩溃，商品货币（尤其是香烟）广泛流通。香烟因易于分割和国际接受度高，成为事实上的交换媒介，能买到纸马克买不到的商品。香烟被视为「好货币」而贬值的帝国马克被视为「坏货币」，部分逆转了格雷欣法则。人们也囤积金币和实物以待货币改革。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic
sources.quote: Among these were commodity-based monies, such as a cigarette-based currency. Cigarettes, due to being easily divisible and internationally acceptable, bought goods that paper marks could not. Although never formally declared as legal tender, cigarettes became widely accepted as a medium of exchange. Cigarettes began to be widely viewed as "good money" while the depreciating Reichsmark was seen as "bad money," partially reversing Gresham's law. People also held coins and other tangible goods in anticipation of a currency reform.

fact: 鲁尔占领期间，莱茵-威斯特法伦煤业辛迪加将总部（包括关键的档案和运营计划）迁出占领区，脱离MICUM控制。德国铁路官员和工人罢工并拆毁车站标识和信号箱，法国不得不自带人员接管铁路，花了数月才使其正常运转。鲁尔煤炭外运量降到低于占领前法国获得的水平。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Occupation of the Ruhr
sources.quote: The situation for the French was further complicated by the fact that the Rhenish-Westphalian Coal Syndicate moved its headquarters (including, crucially, its archives and operational plans) out of the occupied district and thus from control by MICUM. Coal taken out of the Ruhr dropped to less than the French had been receiving previous to the occupation. The Germans also stopped importing iron ore, which caused significant financial losses in the French iron mining region of Lorraine.
